title: Suffix Search Computation
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a Boolean, let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words, and let $x,b$ be finite Boolean words. Let $p,B$ be natural numbers and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of fourteen registers, with every register value at most $B$. Suppose register $0$ contains $4|x|+4$, register $3$ contains twice the length of $\langle x,b\rangle$, register $13$ contains $2|f(x)|+2$, and register $5$ contains $p$. Assume also that $2|f(x)|+2\le p$ and $2|f(x)|+2+|b|\le B$. Starting in the suffix-search state with register values $v$, no result yet, and input $\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$, the counter machine halts with result true precisely when $p<2|f(x)|+2+|b|$ if $\mathrm{mode}$ is true; if it is false, the result is the bit of $b$ at index $p-(2|f(x)|+2)$, or false when that index is beyond the end of $b$. Before halting, every configuration satisfies the machine's step-validity condition, and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$v$ assigns natural values to fourteen registers
Every register value of $v$ is at most $B$
